Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About the team

Stripe’s (Startups + Small and Medium Businesses) SSMB Solutions Architecture (SA) team works with technical and business leaders (CTO/ CIO/ CEO/ Founders etc.), payments leaders and product engineering teams in the mid-market segment to evangelize Stripe’s solutions in the market. A solutions architect’s role is to build relationships with decision makers and think strategically about the business needs of Stripe’s customers. Solution Architects identify and propose Stripe solutions to solve complex business challenges and drive growth for our customers. SSMB SAs establish and prescribe best practices around a customer’s strategy, provide business and technical thought leadership and are viewed as a trusted advisor. They work on scaling business processes aligned to maximizing account coverage while working closely with customer and partner resources to deliver a solution that can be adopted quickly. 

What you’ll do

As a member of the team, the Solutions Architect will build highly consultative trusted relationships with c-level executives and technical decision makers in the customer’s organization to provide business and technical thought leadership, and become a trusted advisor in solving mission-critical business challenges. She/he will architect business models with them so they can drive new monetization opportunities and growth for both the user and Stripe. 

Responsibilities

  • Drive thought leadership and build executive relationships with key business and technical stakeholders including CIO, CTO, COO, CRO, CDO & Head of Payments. Strive to become their trusted advisor.
  • Work to deeply understand the customer’s business objectives and apply Stripe’s payments, SaaS, Banking-as-a-Service and Link Network solutions to customer challenges 
  • Secure the technical win for Stripe’s products by delivering demos, responding to RFPs, evangelizing Stripe’s products, and collaborating internally on narratives that align with the customer’s goals.
  • Creating scalable processes (1:M customer engagements, Webinars, office hours etc), partnerships (with external and internal partners) and scaled assets (reusable videos/ templates) in order to act as a force-multiplier in the sales process.  
  • Expand Stripe’s footprint within existing accounts to new global markets and business units by introducing new capabilities and local payment methods
  • Collaborate with multiple internal stakeholders including go-to-market, product and marketing to deliver impactful EBC briefings for SSMB accounts
  • Act as the voice of the customer to inform our product team on insights, trends, and opportunities across our SSMB accounts.
  • Work closely with professional services and partners to accelerate activations and time to live
  • Collaborate with partners to help Stripe scale and reach its Total Addressable Market
  • Approximately 25% travel is anticipated to help you connect in-person in a meaningful way with users and collaborate internally

Who you are

We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement. An ideal candidate should have experience working for medium to large  software companies (preferably in In payment-tech), focused on identifying business priorities, technology strategy, and solution design.They will have demonstrated the ability to become a trusted advisor to senior executives and facilitate customer success including business value identification(discovery/ demo cycles), road mapping, as well as advising and defining successful execution strategies. Ideal candidates have external customer-facing experience, have payment expertise (preferred but not required) who can present and architect Stripe’s solutions, and persuade decision makers to leverage Stripe technology to drive business value. Candidates have previous experience in web architecture, enterprise architecture or experience defining and optimizing financial business processes.  

Minimum requirements

  • 2+ years of experience in a similar customer-facing engineering role (e.g. solutions architect, sales engineer, customer success, professional services delivery) for a fin-tech/payment-tech / global software enterprise with 5+ years of total relevant experience (software development, enterprise sales/ architecture, business development etc.)
  • Experience as a customer facing roles - presenting and architecting solutions. Domain experience in the payments space is preferred 
  • Deep understanding or background in writing code in at least 2 of Stripe’s primary deployment languages (Ruby, Python, JavaScript, Java, Go, etc.) 
  • Outstanding oral and written communication skills, presentation skills, and comfortable explaining complex concepts to both technical and non-technical audiences
  • Able and willing to learn Stripe solutions (Payments, Billing, Connect, etc.) 
  • Ability  to understand how a wide variety of technologies and systems interact with each other (ERP, CRM, Billing, Tax, Legacy)

  • Strong organizational/time management skills and the ability to juggle competing priorities while working with multiple opportunities and customers.

About Polymarket

Polymarket is the world's largest prediction market platform, where people trade on the outcomes of real-world events. As our markets, volumes, and derivative product suite grow, so does the sophistication of the risk infrastructure behind them. Our clearing and risk systems must operate with the rigor of a traditional clearinghouse while moving at the speed of a crypto-native trading platform.

The Role

We're hiring a mid-level quantitative risk analyst to design and implement enterprise-scale risk models at the heart of our clearing operation. You'll own models for market risk, volatility and correlation of derivatives, stress testing, and automated liquidation — the systems that keep the platform solvent and users protected in fast-moving markets.

This is a hands-on role: you'll be building models in production code, not just specifying them. We expect you to work fluently with AI tools for development and research — and to be the skeptic in the room, pressure-testing AI-generated models and code against well-established risk frameworks before anything ships.

What You'll Do

  • Design, implement, and maintain enterprise-scale risk models covering market risk, margin, and counterparty exposure for a clearing organization.

  • Build volatility and correlation models for derivatives, including calibration, backtesting, and ongoing model validation.

  • Develop and run stress-testing frameworks: historical scenarios, hypothetical shocks, and reverse stress tests.

  • Design and tune auto-liquidation logic — trigger thresholds, liquidation waterfalls, and safeguards against cascading liquidations.

  • Use AI tools extensively to accelerate model development, coding, and research — and rigorously validate AI outputs against established risk models (VaR/ES, SPAN-style margining, GARCH-family volatility models, standard correlation frameworks) before deployment.

  • Monitor model performance in production, investigate breaks, and iterate quickly.

  • Partner with engineering, trading, and product teams to embed risk controls into platform architecture.

  • Document model assumptions, limitations, and validation results to an audit-ready standard.

What We're Looking For

  • 5–7 years of quantitative risk experience at a clearinghouse, exchange, prime broker, trading firm, or similar.

  • Proven expertise designing and implementing risk models at enterprise scale — production systems, not just research prototypes.

  • Deep experience modeling volatility, correlation, option skews, option pricing and implementing at scale for trad-fi derivatives, perpetuals, and fully collateralized event contracts.

  • Hands-on experience with market risk modeling, stress testing, and auto-liquidation mechanics in a clearing context.

  • Strong fluency with AI-assisted development and coding, paired with the judgment to pressure-test AI outputs against well-established risk models and catch what looks plausible but is wrong.

  • Expert-level Python (numerical stack: NumPy, pandas, SciPy; solid software engineering practices).

  • Advanced degree in a quantitative field (math, statistics, physics, financial engineering, CS) or equivalent experience.

  • Strong mathematical foundation in stochastic calculus and linear algebra.

Nice to Have

  • C# and/or C++ for performance-critical or production systems.

  • Familiarity with crypto market structure, perpetuals, or prediction markets.

  • Experience with CCP risk frameworks (CPMI-IOSCO PFMI, default management, margin methodology).

  • Experience building real-time risk systems.

Pay Transparency

Base salary range: $400,000 to $450,000, plus equity and benefits.

This is a good-faith range for the level we're hiring at. Experience varies widely within a title here, so if your expectations fall outside it, reach out anyway. We're always happy to talk it through.

Location & Work Setup

This role is based in our New York City office, in person. You'll be working directly alongside the trading, engineering, and risk teams.

We’re hiring a Customer Engineering Lead to own the customer experience end to end: understanding what customers need, designing a path forward, translating requirements into engineering work, and driving delivery through launch and ongoing operations.

You’ll combine strong DeFi fundamentals, practical software engineering skills, and exceptional communication. Customers should trust you to understand their business and technical constraints. Engineers should trust you to bring clear requirements, informed judgment, and well-scoped work.

THE ROLE

You will be the primary owner of customer engagements, from technical discovery and onboarding through production launch and ongoing success. You’ll lead customer conversations, investigate issues directly, organize the work required across Veda, and stay accountable until the customer’s needs are met.

This is a hands-on role with responsibility for building the customer engineering function. You’ll work closely with engineering, product, and growth to make customer delivery more predictable and turn recurring work into repeatable processes.

RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Own customer relationships and communication. Build trust with technical and business stakeholders, lead regular conversations, communicate progress proactively, and address concerns before they escalate. Make sure customers know what is happening, what decisions are needed, and what comes next.

  • Lead technical discovery and solution design. Understand each customer’s goals, architecture, and operational constraints. Map those requirements to Veda’s capabilities, explain tradeoffs, and identify gaps that require product or engineering decisions.

  • Translate requests into actionable engineering work. Produce clear specifications and tickets covering expected behavior, technical context, dependencies, acceptance criteria, and open questions. Resolve ambiguity before it creates unnecessary implementation work.

  • Drive delivery from intake through acceptance. Establish owners and milestones with engineering, coordinate dependencies, surface risks early, and validate that delivered functionality meets the customer’s requirements.

  • Own ongoing customer success. Stay close to adoption, satisfaction, and changing requirements after launch. Coordinate customer communication during incidents and follow through on resolution and corrective actions.

  • Use AI to improve execution. Apply AI tools to research, debugging, specification development, documentation, and workflow automation. Verify outputs and remain accountable for technical accuracy and customer commitments.

YOU HAVE

  • Strong DeFi and Web3 fundamentals. You understand smart contracts, wallets, token approvals, vaults, lending, liquidity, and deposit and withdrawal mechanics, including their operational risks and tradeoffs.

  • Hands-on experience with block explorers and blockchain tooling. You can inspect transactions and events, read contract interfaces and relevant Solidity code, and reason about permissions and the movement of assets.

  • Practical software engineering skills. You can work with APIs and SDKs, read an unfamiliar codebase, write scripts in a language such as Python or TypeScript, and investigate issues across onchain and offchain systems.

  • Exceptional written and verbal communication. You can lead a technical discussion with customer engineers, explain a tradeoff to a business stakeholder, and write a specification that an engineering team can act on.

  • Strong execution and organizational judgment. You can turn an ambiguous request into a concrete plan, manage competing priorities, and drive work across teams through completion.

  • The confidence to set realistic expectations, challenge assumptions constructively, and distinguish confirmed facts from questions that still need investigation.

  • Experience using AI tools in real workflows, with the technical judgment to evaluate and correct their output.

EVEN BETTER IF YOU HAVE

  • Built or supported DeFi vaults, institutional crypto integrations, or products involving lending, staking, or cross-chain infrastructure.

  • Worked directly with exchanges, wallets, asset managers, or other enterprise crypto customers.

  • Created implementation playbooks, intake systems, or automation that improved delivery across multiple customers.

  • Shipped production software or smart contracts and supported them after launch.

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

Customers have a technically credible partner who understands their needs and follows through. Engineering receives clear, validated requirements. Launches become more predictable, recurring issues become less frequent, and customer feedback informs product decisions.

You’ll help define how Veda works with its customers as we grow, with substantial ownership over both individual engagements and the systems that make great delivery repeatable.

Competitive salary and equity, with compensation reflecting experience, technical depth, and the scope of responsibility.

descriptions.job-0nth22p:
Work from anywhere, impact everywhere 

Diversity is at the heart of who we are at Xapo Bank.
We’re a fully distributed team of over 160 Xapiens that work remotely from 50+ countries around the world.

Our beginning: A world that enjoys economic freedom and wealth protection,no matter where you live or who is running your country.
To achieve that, we search the world for the best people for the job.
We work hard, think globally, and inspire each other to learn and grow.
We are committed to changing the way things are done.

Although we are headquartered in Gibraltar, this is a full time, 100% remote position 
Work from anywhere!

Position overview

Xapo's product suite has grown from a Bitcoin vault into a full member proposition: BTC and USD accounts that pay interest, a global card with Bitcoin cashback, Bitcoin-backed loans, a growing suite of BTC wealth and credit products, and access to stocks, ETFs, and stablecoins, all inside one regulated relationship. 

Xapo is a bank, and a bank earns on the money its members choose to hold with it. Each of those products shipped well. What hasn't yet existed is a single owner of the economics of the customer relationship: one person accountable for winning the right members, growing what they hold with us, and keeping them, and for the balance-sheet products that make that possible.

The Chief Customer Officer is a new role at the top of the house, reporting to the CEO. You will run the stream that grows what members hold with Xapo, and you will own the Customer P&L, retail and institutional. It brings growth, client coverage, product management, and product design under one leader who is judged on customer contribution, the assets attracted and kept, and the members who stay. This is a customer-focused role in the most commercial sense: what a member earns from us, not the feature we shipped, is the centre of every decision.

The measure of success is a Customer P&L that grows on what members hold and keep: LTV:CAC improving, approved-to-paid rising, churn falling, and customer contribution the business can plan against.

This is a banking role, not a requirements-gathering role, a marketing role, or a role you can run from a dashboard. Products are priced on the balance sheet and judged on the money they attract and keep.

The mandate

  1. Own the Customer P&L, retail and institutional.
    You own customer contribution: customer gross profit from what members' balances earn, secured lending, Bitcoin yield, and conversion, stocks and ETFs, less the cost of winning and keeping members. We earn on what members hold, not on what they tap, send, or click, so you run on assets held and the margin they earn, not payment volume. Good looks like a Customer P&L the Exco and Board can plan against, where every line has a number you own and can explain, up or down.
  2. Grow what members hold with us, through earning products run like a banker would.
    You own the roadmap for the balance-sheet products: deposits and savings, lending and credit, and trading and structured. Each is led by a mission PM who is a banker, owning a product's contribution and its price on the balance sheet, not a backlog. Requirements go through the gate; the economics are the job. Every item is priced by Finance before it is built, on a shared risk appetite with Risk and Treasury. Good looks like products that scale assets held and member lifetime value at a risk profile the Board actually approved.
  3. Win the right members, efficiently.
    You own Growth: audience, lifecycle, and content, with one head accountable for the path from approval to paid. You own CAC and approved-to-paid, find the members who bring other members, and activate them in week one. Every incentive is priced before it runs. Good looks like net paid-member growth that improves every quarter, at a CAC that LTV comfortably justifies, because you diagnosed where the funnel leaks rather than spending more to fill it.
  4. Keep members, and deepen the relationship with the ones who hold balances.
    Retention is the most efficient growth we have. You own churn, and you own Client Coverage: relationship managers who sell the missions' products to the members who hold balances, and loop demand back into the roadmap. You are accountable for net new AUM flow, covered-book retention, and products per covered member, and for growth that is broad-based rather than concentrated in a few accounts. Good looks like falling churn and AUM growth from members who stay and expand rather than members re-acquired at cost.
  5. Make the value of Xapo visible, and the experience effortless.
    You own Product Design: one design system and one shell, so that members see the value of what they are earning clearly and early, and find every task simple. You design the proposition in the stream with Finance and partner with Operations, who run onboarding, KYC, support, cards, and payments, to remove friction at the points that affect members most. Good looks like members who understand their return, complete what they set out to do, and stay.
  6. Build one Customer organisation, not four.
    Growth, Client Coverage, Mission PMs, and Product Design come together under one operating model: one set of key results read weekly from one source, shared frameworks for discovery and prioritisation, and real career paths for the people in it. Engineering is pulled to a single ranked roadmap, and nobody in your line has engineers of their own. Good looks like fewer hand-offs per outcome and a number for every cell that its owner explains every week.
  7. Bring the regulated-bank and crypto-native lens to every customer call.
    You understand that a KYC onboarding decision and an AML monitoring decision carry different risk appetites, that a false positive at the gate is a paid-for member lost, and that a proposition built for a crypto-native power user can still fail a first-time bank customer. You can sit in the same room as a CRO, an MLRO, a CFO, and an engineering lead and make a customer case that survives all four conversations.

How you'll operate

This part matters as much as the mandate. The known failure mode for this role, in any company, is a CCO with a polished customer-insight deck and no ownership of the number. That is disqualifying here.

  • You lead from inside the work. You sit in on growth reviews, mission PM reviews, client meetings, and member calls, not just steering committees. PMs, designers, and relationship managers three levels down know your name because you've solved problems with them.
  • You move people with the business case, not the whip. When a priority needs to change, you diagnose the problem, build the case with data and the economics, and show teams why it matters, so they re-prioritise because they're convinced, not because they were told. Your authority comes from being right and being useful, not from your title.
  • You have extreme ownership. You own the Customer P&L and the member metrics beneath it, not the feature ship date. If a launch didn't move contribution, LTV:CAC, approved-to-paid, or churn, you don't report "the roadmap item shipped", you change the approach.
  • You have genuine gravitas. Senior, experienced leaders welcome your input because you've earned the standing to give it. You can challenge any executive's plan, including the CEO's, constructively, with evidence, and be thanked for it, because your challenge makes their work stronger.
  • You diagnose before you prescribe. You can walk into a leaking funnel, a churning segment, or a product that isn't earning and find the structural cause, then fix the economics, not just the symptom.

What you'll have done 

  • 10+ years in senior commercial or customer leadership (CCO, Chief Growth or Commercial Officer, MD or Head of Retail or Wealth, or equivalent) in digital banking, fintech, or payments, including meaningful time in a regulated environment (banking licence, e-money, or equivalent prudential/conduct regime).
  • Crypto-native credibility: hands-on experience building and growing customer propositions on or around digital assets, custody, on-chain flows, Bitcoin-backed lending, or similar. You don't need Bitcoin explained to you, and you don't need banking explained to you either.
  • Customer P&L ownership: you have owned a customer or product P&L judged on contribution, balances, and margin rather than transaction volume, and you are fluent in NIM, unit economics, customer contribution, and LTV:CAC.
  • Growth and lifecycle: a track record of acquiring, activating, and retaining members in a regulated, KYC-heavy environment, improving approved-to-paid and churn while holding CAC to a level that LTV justifies, not just growth-hacking a free consumer app.
  • Banking-grade product leadership: you have led product management for balance-sheet products such as savings, lending, or structured products, priced with Finance, with PMs who own a product's economics rather than a backlog. Experience with client coverage or relationship-managed models for high-balance and institutional clients is a strong advantage.
  • Commercial and risk fluency: you can build a customer business case that survives scrutiny from Finance, Risk, and Compliance in the same meeting, and you know the difference between growth that's sustainable and growth that's borrowed from tomorrow's risk appetite.
  • A track record of outcomes you can narrate: specific LTV:CAC, approved-to-paid, churn, AUM, or contribution numbers you owned, bets you killed when the data didn't support them, and outcomes you can prove.

The first 90 days

Day 30: The Customer P&L baseline is documented across retail and institutional: customer contribution, LTV:CAC, approved-to-paid, churn, net paid-member growth, and assets attracted and kept. You have formed your own independent view of where members are won, lost, and under-served, and shared it with the CEO and Board.
Day 60: The unified Customer operating model is live: one set of key results across Growth, Client Coverage, Mission PMs, and Product Design, read weekly from one source. Every mission PM owns a product's contribution and its price, and the roadmap is ranked on what it earns, built with Finance and the line leads.
Day 90: At least one measurable improvement in LTV:CAC, approved-to-paid, churn, or net new AUM flow is live and attributable to a change you made, not a feature ship, an outcome moved. Every cell in your line has defined key results and an owner who explains the number every week.

What this role is not

  • Not a requirements-gathering role. Mission PMs are bankers who own a product's contribution and price, not a backlog. You partner with Technology, Finance, and Operations on execution; you don't run those functions.
  • Not a volume role. If your primary output is card spend, transfer volume, or a shipped list rather than assets held and the margin they earn, we have both failed.
  • Not a reporting layer. If your primary output is a customer-insight deck or a roadmap deck, we have both failed.
  • Not a role that can be done from a distance. Remote-first means distributed, not detached.

Other requirements

  • A dedicated workspace.
  • A reliable internet connection with the fastest speed possible in your area.
  • Alignment with Our Values and the Xapo Values-Driven Leadership principles.

Why work for Xapo?

Impact Globally, Work Remotely.

  • Shape the Future
    Improve lives through cutting-edge technology, work 100% remotely from anywhere in the world.

  • Great work-life balance
    Build amazing things with a balance of autonomy and collaborative teamwork. Set your own work schedule and make use of a flexible PTO plan when you need to recharge. 

  • Expect Excellence
    Collaborate, learn, and grow with a high-performance team. Learn how you learn best - from books to conferences, you’ll get a yearly budget for your individual learning and development goals.

At Xapo, we prioritize consumer protection and adhere to regulatory requirements by ensuring that all Xapiens are accountable for upholding principles of fair treatment, transparency, and ethical conduct in their interactions with customers and stakeholders.

What You’ll Do:
